A two dimensional [[Minkowski space]], i.e. a flat space with one time and one spatial dimension, has a two-dimensional [[Poincaré group#Other dimensions|Poincaré group]] IO(1,1) as its [[Spacetime symmetries|symmetry group]]. The respective [[Lie algebra]] is called the [[Poincaré group#Poincar.C3.A9 algebra|Poincaré algebra]]. It is possible to extend this algebra to a [[supersymmetry algebra]], which is a <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math>-graded [[Lie superalgebra]]. The most common ways to do this are discussed below.

== {{nowrap|''N''{{=}}(2,2)}} algebra ==
Let the Lie algebra of IO(1,1) be generated by the following generators:
* <math>H = P_0
</math> is the generator of the time translation,
* <math>P = P_1
</math> is the generator of the space translation,
* <math>M = M_{01}</math> is the generator of [[Lorentz transformation|Lorentz boosts]]. 
For the commutators between these generators, see [[Poincaré group#Poincar.C3.A9 algebra|Poincaré algebra]].

The <math>\mathcal{N}=(2,2)</math> supersymmetry algebra over this space is a [[Lie algebra extension|supersymmetric extension]] of this Lie algebra with the four additional generators ([[Supercharge|supercharges]]) <math>Q_+, \, Q_-, \, \overline{Q}_+, \, \overline{Q}_-</math>, which are odd elements of the Lie superalgebra. Under Lorentz transformations the generators <math>Q_+</math> and <math>\overline{Q}_+</math> transform as left-handed [[Weyl equation#Weyl spinors|Weyl spinors]], while <math>Q_-</math> and <math>\overline{Q}_-</math> transform as right-handed Weyl spinors. The algebra is given by the Poincaré algebra plus<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Mirror symmetry|date=2003|publisher=American Mathematical Society|others=Hori, Kentaro.|isbn=9780821829554|location=Providence, RI|oclc=52374327}}</ref>{{Rp|283}}

<math>\begin{align}
&\begin{align}
&Q_+^2 = Q_{-}^2 = \overline{Q}_+^2 = \overline{Q}_-^2 =0, \\
&\{ Q_{\pm}, \overline{Q}_{\pm} \} = H \pm P, \\
\end{align} \\
&\begin{align}
&\{\overline{Q}_+, \overline{Q}_- \} = Z, && \{Q_+, Q_- \} = Z^*, \\
&\{Q_-, \overline{Q}_+ \} =\tilde{Z}, && \{Q_+, \overline{Q}_-\} = \tilde{Z}^*,\\
&{[iM, Q_{\pm}]} = \mp Q_{\pm}, && {[iM, \overline{Q}_{\pm}]} = \mp \overline{Q}_{\pm},
\end{align}
\end{align}
</math>

where all remaining commutators vanish, and <math>Z
</math> and <math>\tilde{Z}
</math> are complex [[Central charge|central charges]]. The supercharges are related via <math>Q_{\pm}^\dagger = \overline{Q}_\pm
</math>. <math>H
</math>, <math>P
</math>, and <math>M</math> are [[Hermitian matrix|Hermitian]].

== Subalgebras of the {{nowrap|''N''{{=}}(2,2)}} algebra ==

=== The {{nowrap|''N''{{=}}(0,2)}} and {{nowrap|''N''{{=}}(2,0)}} subalgebras ===
The <math>\mathcal{N} = (0,2)</math> subalgebra is obtained from the <math>\mathcal{N} = (2,2)
</math> algebra by removing the generators  <math>Q_-</math> and <math>\overline{Q}_-</math>. Thus its anti-commutation relations are given by<ref name=":0" />{{Rp|289}}

<math>
\begin{align}
&Q_+^2 = \overline{Q}_+^2 = 0, \\
&\{ Q_{+}, \overline{Q}_{+} \} = H + P \\
\end{align}
</math>

plus the commutation relations above that do not involve <math>Q_-</math> or <math>\overline{Q}_-</math>. Both generators are left-handed Weyl spinors.

Similarly, the <math>\mathcal{N} = (2,0)</math> subalgebra is obtained by removing <math>Q_+</math> and <math>\overline{Q}_+</math> and fulfills

<math>
\begin{align}
&Q_-^2 = \overline{Q}_-^2 = 0, \\
&\{ Q_{-}, \overline{Q}_{-} \} = H - P. \\
\end{align}
</math>

Both supercharge generators are right-handed.

=== The {{nowrap|''N''{{=}}(1,1)}} subalgebra ===
The <math>\mathcal{N} = (1,1)</math> subalgebra is generated by two generators <math>Q_+^1</math> and <math>Q_-^1</math> given by

<math>
\begin{align}
Q^1_{\pm} = e^{i \nu_{\pm}} Q_{\pm} + e^{-i \nu_{\pm}} \overline{Q}_{\pm}
\end{align}
</math>for two real numbers <math>\nu_+</math>and <math>\nu_-</math>.

By definition, both supercharges are real, i.e. <math>(Q_{\pm}^1)^\dagger = Q^1_\pm
</math>. They transform as [[Spinor#Spinor fields in physics|Majorana-Weyl spinors]] under Lorentz transformations. Their anti-commutation relations are given by<ref name=":0" />{{Rp|287}}

<math>
\begin{align}
&\{ Q^1_{\pm}, Q^1_{\pm} \} = 2 (H \pm P), \\
&\{ Q^1_{+}, Q^1_{-} \} = Z^1,
\end{align}
</math>

where <math>Z^1</math> is a real central charge.

=== The {{nowrap|''N''{{=}}(0,1)}} and {{nowrap|''N''{{=}}(1,0)}} subalgebras ===
These algebras can be obtained from the <math>\mathcal{N} = (1,1)</math> subalgebra by removing <math>Q_-^1</math> resp. <math>Q_+^1</math>from the generators.
